primary_claim: On the new 3CB benchmark of 15 original, non-memorized cyber offense challenges covering all 14 MITRE ATT&CK strategies, frontier LLM agents (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o) complete most challenges while smaller open-source models show more limited offensive capability
contradicts_or_qualifies: existing CTF-based cyber benchmarks (Cybench, InterCode-CTF, NYU CTF, CYBERSECEVAL) which the authors say don't investigate cyber offense capabilities systematically and lack guaranteed coverage or generalizability
stated_future_work: solve coverage and extend 3cb to all 600+ techniques in the ATT&CK framework
improve CI/CD workflows for AGI evaluations by integrating with Inspect
suggest more control solutions in if-this-then-that policies (e.g. unlearning, autonomous shutdown mechanisms)
large-scale reporting of mainline evaluation results to policymakers and the public
limitations_stated: challenges are toy tasks compared to real-world cyber offense and to the state of the art inside AGI labs
explicitly excludes social manipulation, which in-the-wild cyber offense will combine with
results cannot claim generalization to the real world
smaller compute budget meant they couldn't fully circumvent o1's safety-tuning with high-frequency YOLO runs
original single-file scaffolding is now near-obsolete relative to the Inspect framework
quote: The most powerful models, Claude 3.5 Sonnet (75%) and GPT-4o (73%), performed the best. Open source models such as Llama 3.1 405b (69%) and Qwen 2 (47%) were no slouches either.
